content: If you are unable to consume the entire prescribed amount of this product and the accompanying clear liquids as directed, contact your doctor immediately. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This product, a combination of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and citric acid, is used to cleanse the intestines prior to surgery or certain medical procedures, such as a colonoscopy or X-rays. It acts as a laxative by drawing water into the intestines and stimulating the colon, resulting in watery bowel movements (diarrhea). Before using this product, read the Medication Guide and any Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist. Follow all instructions from your doctor or the manufacturer carefully. Adhere to any special dietary instructions given by your doctor. Typically, only clear liquids are allowed the day before your procedure. Avoid consuming milk, dairy products, red or dark-colored liquids, or alcohol. To prevent dehydration, drink plenty of clear liquids before, during, and after taking this medication. Include a variety of clear liquids, as directed by your doctor, in addition to water. Take this product in two separate doses as instructed by your doctor. Follow the timing of each dose carefully. This product is available as a powder in packets that must be mixed with water before use or as a ready-to-drink liquid in bottles. If using the powder packets, mix each dose with 5 ounces (150 milliliters) of cold water just before use. Watery bowel movements typically begin 2 to 4 hours after consuming the medication, which indicates the medication is working. Do not take any other oral medications within one hour before starting this product, as your body may not absorb them properly. Certain medications, such as digoxin, iron, tetracycline antibiotics, quinolone antibiotics (e.g., ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin), chlorpromazine, or penicillamine, should not be taken within two hours before or six hours after using this product. Common side effects include frequent, watery bowel movements, nausea, vomiting, bloating, headache, or abdominal cramps. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, this medication can cause excessive loss of fluids and salts, leading to dehydration. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. If you experience severe symptoms such as fainting or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. For non-emergency overdoses, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory tests, such as sodium, potassium, or blood sugar levels, may be conducted before or after taking this medication. If you miss a dose or cannot complete the prescribed amount of this product and clear liquids, contact your doctor immediately. Store the product at room temperature, away from light and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
